parts.latex: Which of the following could represent the graph of $y = -x^2 + 1$?

solutions.latex:
The graph of $y=-x^2+1$ is a parabola, since $x$ is squared.

The coefficient of $x^2$ is negative, so it is concave down.

The $y$-intercept is found by letting $x=0$:
$$y=1$$
The $x$-intercepts are found by letting $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned} -x^2+1 &= 0 \\ x^2 &= 1 \\ x &= \pm 1 \end{aligned}$$
So the graph is a concave down parabola with $y$-intercept $1$ and $x$-intercepts $-1$ and $1$. Only graph C has these features (A is a line, B is exponential, D is a hyperbola).

$$\therefore\ \text{the graph is C}$$

solutions.latex: The height and area cannot be negative, so only the part of the graph with $h>0$ can be used.

Set $A=8$ in $A=0.5h^2+3h$:
$$\begin{aligned} 0.5h^2+3h &= 8 \\ h^2+6h-16 &= 0 \\ (h+8)(h-2) &= 0 \end{aligned}$$

Each equal side $x$ is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle with sides $2$ and $4$ (half the base):
$$x^2=2^2+4^2$$
so $x=\sqrt{20}$.
$$\begin{aligned} P &= \sqrt{20}+\sqrt{20}+8 \\ &= 16.9 \text{ cm} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the slant side, or equivalent merit

The wall forms one side, so the fence is two sides of length $x$ and one of length $y$. The wire is 16 m.
$$\begin{aligned} 2x+y &= 16 \\ y &= 16-2x \end{aligned}$$
The area of the rectangle is $A=xy$.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= x(16-2x) \\ &= 16x-2x^2 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ y=16-2x \text{ and } A=16x-2x^2$$

Draw the horizontal line $A=24$ on the graph. It meets the curve where $x=2$ and where $x=6$.

Check: $16(2)-2(2)^2=24$ and $16(6)-2(6)^2=24$.

Find $y$ from $y=16-2x$.
$$\begin{aligned} x=2:\quad y &= 16-4=12 \\ x=6:\quad y &= 16-12=4 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ x=2 \text{ m with } y=12 \text{ m, or } x=6 \text{ m with } y=4 \text{ m}$$
criteria: Finds both values of $x$ ($2$ and $6$), or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:

$$\begin{aligned} y &= 16-2(4) \\ &= 8 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ x=4 \text{ m and } y=8 \text{ m, giving the maximum area of } 32 \text{ m}^2$$

To determine the maximum area ($A$) of a rectangle with a perimeter of 30 m, Melanie sketched the following diagrams in her notebook.

\exfigure{1265_q15_1}

The point $A$ is at the turning point on the parabolic graph.

Melanie correctly determined the maximum area of the rectangle (in square metres) by finding the value of $A$.

What is this value?

solutions.latex:
The perimeter is 30 m, so the sides are $x$ and $15-x$, and the area is:
$$A=x(15-x)=15x-x^2$$
The graph is a downward parabola with $x$-intercepts $0$ and $15$, so its turning point is at the midpoint $x=\dfrac{0+15}{2}=7.5$.

Maximum area:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 7.5\times(15-7.5) \\ &= 7.5\times 7.5 \\ &= 56.25 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ A=56.25 \text{ (option C)}$$

At the same time as the stone is thrown, Jay releases a toy glider from the top of the tower.

The glider drifts down, losing height at a constant rate of 5 metres each second.

Draw the graph modelling the height of the glider on the grid on the previous page and determine the equation which describes the model. Label the graph Glider.
Determine the height of the glider when the stone reaches the ground.

solutions.latex:
Find key points of $h = 20t - 5t^2 + 60$.

The $h$-intercept is $h = 60$ at $t = 0$. The stone reaches the ground when $h = 0$:
$$\begin{aligned} -5t^2 + 20t + 60 &= 0 \\ t^2 - 4t - 12 &= 0 \\ (t-6)(t+2) &= 0 \end{aligned}$$
So $t = 6$, as $t \ge 0$.

The axis of symmetry is $t = \dfrac{-20}{2(-5)} = 2$, and the maximum height is
$$\begin{aligned} h(2) &= 40 - 20 + 60 \\ &= 80 \end{aligned}$$
Table of values:
$$\begin{array}{c|ccccccc} t & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 \\ \hline h & 60 & 75 & 80 & 75 & 60 & 35 & 0 \end{array}$$
\exfigure{264_q24_s1}

The glider starts at the top of the tower ($h = 60$ when $t = 0$) and loses 5 metres each second, so the height decreases at a constant rate $5$ m/s. This is a straight line with gradient $-5$ and $h$-intercept $60$.
$$h = 60 - 5t$$
Points: $(0, 60)$ and $(6, 30)$.

\exfigure{264_q24_s2}
$$\therefore\ \text{The glider model is } h = 60 - 5t.$$
criteria: Gives the equation or draws the line, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The stone reaches the ground when $t = 6$ (from part (a)).

Height of the glider at that time:
$$\begin{aligned} h &= 60 - 5(6) \\ &= 30 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{The glider is } 30 \text{ metres above the ground.}$$
